chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: KSTP radio in Minneapolis and Wefland's encouragement
summary: Hired for Sunday radio shows, Norvo plays Lucky Strike-style triplets, and Wefland urges him to develop his four-hammer and legato playing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: -- I went from there over to KSDP, a guy by the name of Stan Hubbard used to come and hear me, and he knew I could -- he was crazy about the Lucky Strike dance

orchestra. And so he said will you come over and work on Sunday's. I have a program. By that time, Weflin, his home was in Minneapolis, and he was a drummer back at the station, the guy that was sobered up. And he was my biggest booster, so all I had to do was Sunday night, I'd go over and when they played these -- they played classical things, there was a director by the name of Hymie Wentler, who was the first flutist with the Minneapolis Symphony. But they'd play jazz tunes and when they'd do that, the first indication it was jazz was when Red Norvo would play these triplets and everthing like they had on Lucky Strike.
So he -- Hubbard thought I was the greatest cause I could do that.
Like the guy on Lucky Strike.

So I stayed there for most of that winter. I stayed in Minneapolis. And all that time Weflin was encouraging me. I could play In a Mist on rhumba. And he's say 'Nobody plays like that. Using four hammers, like you do. You should work on those things and write things. Develop that. Nobody's developed that technique like that.' And he said, 'Not only that, but when you play jazz, you got a touch that none of us have got.' He said, 'It's -- and you can play legato, and he said, 'I've never heard anybody legato on xylophone. He said,
"I don't know how you do it," he said, "What do you do?"
I said, "I don't really know except that I think legato when I'm playing."
He said, "Well maybe that's it." And he was a good xylophone player.
